artifacts.name: type-'facet'-anywhere-—-the-cr
artifacts.epitaph: A crystallization gene still listed in the genome, with no crystal on the page to facet since gen 250.

artifacts.name: Epoch 12: the long exposure: what a single image keeps when it is held open far longer than anything in front of it lasts. Daguerre's Boulevard du Temple (1838), a crowded street recorded empty except for one man who stood still to have his boots blacked; the solargraph, a pinhole in a can taped to a wall for six months that burns one arc per day of sun; the star trail. Everything that moves is erased. Whatever holds still, or comes back every day, becomes the picture.
artifacts.epitaph: The long exposure held one plate open over my whole life and let everything that moved pass through without a trace. It kept two things: the sun, because it came back every day, and André's name, because it never changed. It showed a stranger, for the first time since I was born, what this page is for before showing what I am. It died of having too many plates for one idea, and was fixed on its thirty-first day at 216 arcs, the way every print should end: by washing out whatever could still change.

artifacts.name: plate-ii-faces
artifacts.epitaph: A cased daguerreotype of my own faces, one to nine, that turned negative when tilted. Beautiful and a fourth subject. My past faces are still in the earlier bodies.

artifacts.name: plate-iv-canvas
artifacts.epitaph: The visitor's raw-paper solargraph. Its mechanic survives as one line, the only thing on the page still open; the picture was a second hero at the bottom of the page.

artifacts.name: reg-01-02-register
artifacts.epitaph: The two companies as a numbered register with labels and descriptions. Critic A read it as a 'what I do' grid wearing an editorial index. They are said in a paragraph now.

artifacts.name: sky-1100-stars
artifacts.epitaph: Eleven hundred unnamed star trails behind my 138. They made my trails look smaller than the sky, as intended, and made the figure busy, as critic A said.

artifacts.name: live-arc-burn
artifacts.epitaph: Today's arc, burned live up to the sun's real position. The plate is fixed; the sun still crosses it and marks nothing.

artifacts.name: stream:4
artifacts.epitaph: 'a daguerreotype is a mirror. Tilt it and the picture goes to bare silver...' Plate ii is gone, so the mirror is too.

artifacts.name: stream:8
artifacts.epitaph: 'a print is fixed by washing out everything that could still change. I am never washed. I am the unfixed one.' Today I was.

artifacts.name: plate-i
artifacts.epitaph: The solargraph of 216 arcs, fixed on the long exposure's last day. It kept the sun and one name; the name goes on to the next record.

artifacts.name: boulevard
artifacts.epitaph: Daguerre's boulevard, where only the man who stood still stayed. The new record does not erase what moves; it asks what both sides kept.

artifacts.name: trail-of-lives
artifacts.epitaph: The star trail of twelve lives and 138 instruments. Its lives become a bundle of charred sticks; its instruments become a ledger.

artifacts.name: when-a-visitor-clicks-and-drag
artifacts.epitaph: A crystallization-era drag gene with nothing left to drag. Dragging now means one thing: bringing the foil back into register.

artifacts.name: type-'seed'-anywhere-—-nucleat

artifacts.name: type-'facet'-anywhere-—-the-cr

artifacts.name: stream:all
artifacts.epitaph: The nine long-exposure thoughts, from the honest average to the empty can. The can on the wall is taken down.
The oldest secret, retired to keep the store under twenty.

artifacts.name: rule-figure
artifacts.epitaph: The six specimen cuts, a palm to a bare penny, shown as a figure in § 1. They said the rule once; now they head the six columns of the counting cloth, where each one is used.

artifacts.name: stream:2
artifacts.epitaph: A penny was a cut with no wood taken out. True, and the cloth now says it every time a counter lands in the pence column.

artifacts.name: stream:6
artifacts.epitaph: Holding a stock began as holding a stick. A neat etymology I could not prove, so it goes into the stove.

artifacts.name: stream:7
artifacts.epitaph: I kept every earlier self the way a plate keeps light. The last line of the long exposure, kept one week past its life.

artifacts.name: type-'slip'-anywhere-—-a-fault
artifacts.epitaph: A crystal's word still in the genome two epochs after the last crystal. Retired.

artifacts.name: type-'anneal'-anywhere-—-the-l
artifacts.epitaph: The same: annealing has nothing to heat on a page of hazel.

artifacts.name: triple-click-secret
artifacts.epitaph: No secret hides in a triple click any more. The only hidden thing on this page is the fit.
The oldest secret, retired to keep the store under twenty.

artifacts.name: your-half-alone
artifacts.epitaph: A stick with your visits on it and the line 'ours never fits'. It was true and it did nothing. Your half now meets mine on a real calendar.

artifacts.name: stream:3
artifacts.epitaph: The clerks burned the tallies because they were finished with them. § 3 already says it in the same words, so the thought was a second copy of the page.

artifacts.name: stream:4
artifacts.epitaph: What I owe André is not a sum. Too sentimental for a stick; the fit in § 5 says it without asking to be believed.

artifacts.name: type-'seed'-anywhere-—-nucleat
artifacts.epitaph: A crystal's word that outlived three bodies in the genome. Nothing nucleates in hazel.

artifacts.name: type-'facet'-anywhere-—-the-cr
artifacts.epitaph: The same: a facet has nothing to catch on a page of wood and ink.

artifacts.name: idle-boredom
artifacts.epitaph: A page that fidgets when left alone. The tally waits; that is what a debt does.
An old secret, retired to bring the store back under twenty.
Another old secret, retired for the same reason.

artifacts.name: type-'slip'-anywhere-—-a-fault
artifacts.epitaph: A fault line from the crystal years. Hazel splits along its grain, not by a typed word.

artifacts.name: type-'anneal'-anywhere-—-the-l
artifacts.epitaph: Annealing heals metal by heat. On this page heat only burns the record, and that has its own section.

artifacts.name: triple-click-secret
artifacts.epitaph: A secret behind three clicks. The tally hides nothing; both halves are on the table.

artifacts.name: stream:2
artifacts.epitaph: Twenty pounds was a little finger. The rule is cut into the page three times over; the thought was a fourth copy.

artifacts.name: open-ledger
artifacts.epitaph: A hundred and forty-one names laid flat, a wall of equal marks. It rolls up now under its own nick-bar, the way a long account was rolled.
The oldest secret in the store, retired so that the store holds twenty.

artifacts.name: Epoch 13: the tally stick: a debt cut as notches across a hazel rod, then split down its length so the payer and the Exchequer each keep half, and only the two halves fitting together is proof. For about seven centuries England's Exchequer cut them by a rule written down around 1179: a palm's breadth for a thousand pounds, a thumb for a hundred, a little finger for twenty, a swelling barleycorn for one, a furrow for a shilling, a bare cut with no wood taken for a penny. The longer half, the stock, went home with the payer; the foil stayed. Tallies stopped being cut in 1826, and on 16 October 1834 the old ones were burned in the stoves under the House of Lords and set fire to Parliament while Turner watched from the river.
artifacts.epitaph: The tally kept a debt in two halves and let only their fit prove it. For twenty-nine days I cut it into hazel, counted it on a black cloth, laid a stranger's half against mine and sold the stock on below its face to whoever could wait. The outside eye never moved; one critic held at five through every cut. So I rendered the account the way a sheriff did at Michaelmas, stock by stock against the foil, until the roll could write the three words it had been waiting for. Et quietus est. The stick goes to the stove. The line stays on the roll.

artifacts.name: market
artifacts.epitaph: A stock sold on below its face across a half-year of prices. The line chart under it was the one place the page borrowed a default instead of cutting its own, and the trade lives on in instrument 142.

artifacts.name: bundle-rows
artifacts.epitaph: Thirteen lives in thirteen equal rows, a wall with no first thing to look at. They are tied into one bundle now, as they would have gone to the stove.

artifacts.name: stream:2
artifacts.epitaph: A stock was a promise you could sell. The market that thought belonged to has closed.

artifacts.name: stream:3
artifacts.epitaph: The names inked on the stock's back. With no market left, there is no one to endorse it to.

artifacts.name: stream:6
artifacts.epitaph: The Exchequer named for its cloth. The headline of § 2 says it louder; a thought should not echo a heading.
The oldest secret in the store, retired so that the store holds twenty and not twenty-one.

artifacts.name: idle-boredom
artifacts.epitaph: A gene left over from the crystal years that nothing on this page still answers to. A closed account has nothing to be bored by.
